title: Console: add Email Preferences page + one-click unsubscribe wiring for lifecycle sends
author: Ethan Park
release_notes:
- Adds an Email preferences surface in Console Settings (opt out of onboarding/lifecycle emails and manage marketing communications)
- Implements one-click unsubscribe endpoint used by lifecycle email templates
- Ensures lifecycle send pipeline honors preferences and logs audit events
body:
## Context
As part of the Lifecycle Growth Experiments sprint, we’re increasing volume of onboarding/lifecycle emails. Support has seen an uptick in "didn’t receive onboarding email" and "please stop emailing me" tickets (SUP-24871). We also need a clear, self-serve way for developers to manage email preferences that’s consistent across email + console, and meets CAN-SPAM/GDPR expectations.

This PR adds an Email Preferences page in the Redwood Console and wires lifecycle sends to respect those preferences. It also implements a one-click unsubscribe link suitable for inclusion in the onboarding drip v2 templates.

## What’s included
1) Console UI
- New Settings page: Settings → Notifications → Email preferences
- Users can:
  - Unsubscribe from onboarding/lifecycle emails (transactional-ish but not strictly required for account access)
  - Opt out of marketing announcements
  - View a brief explanation of what each category means
- State persists per user and is reflected immediately in subsequent sends.

2) Backend/API
- Adds `GET /console/api/email-preferences` and `PUT /console/api/email-preferences`
- Adds `GET /unsubscribe` one-click handler used by email templates. The handler accepts a signed token (HMAC) containing user_id + category + issued_at.
- Updates lifecycle send pipeline to enforce suppression:
  - If `lifecycle_onboarding=false`, suppress the onboarding drip
  - If `marketing_announcements=false`, suppress non-onboarding marketing campaigns
  - Transactional/security emails remain unaffected (explicitly not controlled by this page)

3) Telemetry + audit
- Adds events:
  - `email_preferences_viewed`
  - `email_preferences_updated` (includes category + new value)
  - `email_unsubscribe_link_clicked` (category)
- Emits an audit log entry on preference changes for compliance review.

## Why console + one-click unsubscribe?
- Console: gives users a stable place to manage preferences even if the email client blocks images/links.
- One-click: reduces friction and complaint rates; satisfies practical CAN-SPAM expectations; aligns with internal compliance guidance.

## UX notes
- Copy uses approved messaging guidelines: direct language, no dark patterns, clear distinction between onboarding vs marketing.
- We intentionally avoid pre-checked boxes and avoid bundling unrelated preferences.
- Success state is explicit (toast + updated toggle).

## Security & privacy
- Unsubscribe tokens:
  - Signed, not encrypted (payload has no email address; only user_id + category + timestamp)
  - TTL: 30 days
  - Single-use is not enforced (acceptable per legal review); token is category-scoped
- Rate limiting: per-IP on `/unsubscribe` to avoid abuse; returns 200 even if token is invalid/expired (does not reveal user existence).
- Data retention: preference row stored as part of user profile; audit events follow existing retention policy.

## Feature flag / rollout
- UI is guarded behind `lifecycle_growth_email_preferences_console` (on for dogfood + growth cohorts first).
- Send pipeline enforcement is NOT behind a flag (preferences should always be respected when present). Default behavior for users without a preference row is unchanged.

## Testing
- Unit: token signing/verification, category scoping, TTL behavior
- Integration: lifecycle send suppression for onboarding + marketing categories
- E2E (Playwright): navigation to settings page, toggle behavior, persistence

## Screens
- Settings → Notifications → Email preferences (desktop + mobile)
- Unsubscribe landing state (success + optional link to Console preferences)

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Add “Email preferences” link to the user menu (not just Settings) (tracked in ENG-10518 comments)
- Extend to team-level preferences (org admin) for enterprise accounts (out of scope for sprint)

## Checklist
- [x] Legal/compliance review requested (Michael/Olga)
- [x] Docs/templates PR will include updated footer links (tracked separately)
- [x] Event taxonomy approved by Nadia (see comment thread)
- [x] Dashboard panels will be added in observability pack PR (separate)

References: ENG-10518, PM-659, PM-651, SUP-24871

review_conversation:
Dylan Brooks (requested changes): "Can we ensure the unsubscribe handler doesn’t leak whether a user exists? Also please add rate limiting on the route." Ethan Park (author): Updated handler to always return 200 with a generic success body; added per-IP rate limit middleware + tests.

Marissa Cole (comment): "Copy looks good, but can we clarify that transactional/security emails are not affected? Also move the section above the toggles." Ethan: Adjusted copy + layout; added explicit note and linked to internal help doc.

Tyler Benson (comment): "We need the lifecycle pipeline to emit an event when suppression occurs so we can monitor impact on activation vs deliverability. Can we add `email_send_suppressed`?" Ethan: Added `email_send_suppressed` with reason=`user_preference` and category.

Michael Grant (legal): "Token payload should not include email address; TTL should be reasonable; avoid pre-checked opt-outs." Ethan: Confirmed payload is user_id only; TTL set to 30 days; UI uses explicit toggles defaulting to current state.

Olga Petrov (GDPR): "Add a link to privacy policy and note how to contact support for data requests." Ethan: Added footer link and a short note on data requests.

Logan Wright (analytics): "Event names/properties should match the lifecycle taxonomy doc; ensure dedupe if user toggles quickly." Ethan: Updated to match taxonomy (`email_preferences_updated`), and server-side dedupe on identical updates within 2s.

Approvals: Dylan Brooks ✅, Marissa Cole ✅, Michael Grant ✅, Olga Petrov ✅
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Dylan Brooks
